name: override_cleared_on_restart
description: A confirmed manual thermostat override is in force when Home Assistant restarts. The restart wipes it: after the restart the override is cleared and no grace is active, so the automation resumes control instead of staying frozen on the occupant's old manual setting (restore_state() is an unconditional clean slate, Issues #199 / #226 / #327).
notes: Replaces grace_timer_expired_on_restart, whose only assertion was the carried-forward classification_applied outcome. That scenario never created an override, so it could not detect a restart that kept one (Issue #1193 review).
Occupant outcome: after a restart the home returns to the automation's comfort schedule instead of staying stuck on a manual override the occupant set hours earlier.

Mechanism: automation.restore_state() unconditionally clears _manual_override_active, _grace_active and _grace_end_time on every restart, not only when the grace had already expired (Issues #199, #226, #327; confirmed by the earlier standalone two-coordinator check recorded in the retired scenario).
manual_grace_seconds is 6000 so the override is still live (grace not expired) at the 21:12 restart: the clear at 21:13 is therefore caused by the restart, not by the grace running out on its own.
The 14:01 classification sets hvac_mode=cool explicitly because build_classification_from_event defaults a missing hvac_mode to off, while classifier.py derives cool for a hot day.
simulate_restart re-runs the engine's restore_state() on the SAME live engine (see run_production.py); the 21:13 temp_update is a no-op reading that advances the scheduler so the clear is emitted.
Revert test: made restore_state() keep _manual_override_active in a scratch copy; override_cleared at 21:13 and the _grace_active/override assertions failed. See the issue #1193 report.

events.note: Hot-day classification: hvac_mode=cool set explicitly (harness default is off; classifier.py derives cool for a hot day).
Occupant switches the thermostat to heat — override detection starts the confirm window.
Confirm window passes with the thermostat still diverging — override confirmed, grace period begins (6000s).
Home Assistant restarts mid-override: restore_state() runs on the engine.
No-op re-assertion of the same readings so the scheduler advances past the restart.

assertions.reason: Thermostat still on heat 10 minutes after the occupant changed it on a hot day — the manual override is confirmed, which is the state the restart must wipe.
An HA restart mid-override clears it: restore_state() is an unconditional clean slate (Issues #199, #226, #327), so the automation resumes instead of being held off by a stale override.
The override's grace period does not survive the restart either (Issues #199, #226, #327): after restore_state() no grace is active, even though 6000s had not elapsed.

verdict.summary: A Home Assistant restart clears a confirmed manual override and its grace period
verdict.observed_behavior: override_confirmed (21:10) -> simulate_restart (21:12) -> override_cleared and no active grace (21:13)
verdict.expected_behavior: restore_state() is a clean slate: no override or grace survives a restart, whether or not the grace had expired (Issues #199, #226, #327)
